title: The direct-image finiteness input holds
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $N$ be an integer prime to
$\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring annihilated by $N$. Then both clauses of the
direct-image finiteness input of
[def-exc-direct-image-input] hold over $k$.

proof.text: Clause (1) follows from [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]. Let $u:S\to T$ be of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes and let $F$ be a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf. Since $N$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}(k)$, it is invertible in $k$, so the theorem applies with the finite ring $A=\Lambda$ annihilated by $N$. Regard $F$ as a constructible complex in degree zero; the theorem gives $Ru_*F$ bounded constructible, and the definition of bounded constructibility then says that each cohomology sheaf $R^qu_*F$ is constructible on $T_{{\mathrm{et}}}$.

For clause (2), let $K$ be a separably closed field of characteristic prime to $N$, let $W$ be a finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension at most $d$, and let $M$ be any torsion sheaf on $W_{{\mathrm{et}}}$. If $W$ is empty, its higher cohomology vanishes immediately. Otherwise write $e=\dim W$; then $e$ is the finite dimension of $W$ and $e\leq d$. The existing separably closed-field bound [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq0$. Applying [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] with $c=0$ and the exact dimension $e$ gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(W)\leq2e$. Since $e\leq d$, this implies the bound $2e\leq2d$; by the defining vanishing condition in [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], $H^q(W,M)=0$ for every $q>2d$. This is clause (2).
